scope: Read-only installed Codex protocol/source audit for the two-role Intent trial.

safety.procedure: Offline help/schema generation and --version only, using the packaged executable, subprocess stdin=DEVNULL, an isolated empty CODEX_HOME, and the existing restricted child_environment helper.

schema_generation.raw_subset_policy: Retain only the five selected generated files. InitializeCapabilities is an embedded definition in the actual v1/InitializeParams.json file; no generated standalone file is claimed.

findings.outcome: Supported by installed primary schema and validated in frozen bridge.
findings.basis: ThreadStartResponse requires top-level model/modelProvider; Thread requires cliVersion/modelProvider. The bridge requires requested model, openai provider at both levels, and installed/admitted CLI0.144.4 before turn/start.

TurnStartResponse and TurnCompletedNotification contain a Turn with no independent served-model field. Completion.model is the confirmed thread-configured model; requested_model/configured_model/model_identity_basis record that distinction, and served_model=null with a reason. This is not a claim that the physical/provider-served model is independently observed.

findings.outcome: Local fixture control behavior validated; live timing unproven.
findings.basis: ServerNotification includes model/rerouted; ErrorNotification includes willRetry. The bridge refuses attributable rerouting or any native error, including willRetry=true, interrupts/closes its owned invocation, and never issues another turn/start. A queued completed notification cannot conceal an already observed reroute/error.

allowProviderModelFallback exists in experimental v2/ThreadStartParams.json and is absent from standard ThreadStartParams. InitializeCapabilities.experimentalApi opts into experimental methods/fields; the native transport advertises false. The current trial bridge omits the experimental request field and validates standard configured identity plus reroute notifications.

The six new model identity fields and core completion keys are reserved. Additional identities are still accepted, so usage_unavailable_reason, cost_unavailable_reason, seed_unavailable_reason, mock and provider_version can be injected into returned/durably retained metadata. Current TrialRunner never supplies those keys and ordinary clients/models cannot call this protected internal API. Root authorized a subsequent strict correlation-identity allowlist correction; that future correction is not part of this frozen candidate.

limitations: The schema audit and protocol fixtures do not establish authenticated native/provider execution or real connected semantic acceptance; those remain BLOCKED.

One model_calls=1 records one native turn/start boundary dispatch. Provider-internal HTTP/model attempts and retry timing are not independently observed or asserted to be exactly one. The adapter halts on the first observed native error and does not replay.
The thread reply confirms native configured model/provider, not an independently observed provider-served model or physical runtime.
Supported real POSIX private IPC/container custody and account readiness require their actual connected evidence; a Windows/local scripted pass is not that evidence.

local_protocol_validation.provider: Explicit protocol fixtures only; actual local custody/lifecycle assertions where specified.

conclusion: Configured-route/rerouting controls and honest unavailable served-model telemetry are implemented and locally validated. Preserve the residual metadata finding for LOCAL-2; no complete acceptance or no-provider-internal-retry claim follows from this observation.
